home.title: Short Final ATC: Live Flights, the air traffic control game
home.description: Short Final ATC is a free air traffic control game for Android with real live flights. Land the real planes at more than 29,000 airports, or try the browser demo.
home.h1: Land the real planes at any airport on Earth.
home.lead: Pick an airport. The real flights landing there arrive at the edge of your screen, under their flight numbers. Draw a path to a runway, keep everyone apart, and land as many as you can.
home.freeNote: Free to play. The daily challenge is always free.
home.statMaps: airports with full maps on this site
home.statOffline: busiest airports open offline in the app
home.feat1Body: Live flights from The OpenSky Network arrive on their real bearing, with their real flight numbers. Simulated planes fill in when the sky is quiet, unless you switch on Real planes only.
home.feat2Body: Search more than 29,000 airports by code, name or city. Each has its real runways, and many have taxiways and gates drawn from OpenStreetMap.
home.feat3Body: The airport's current weather report sets the wind and the active runway, so the approach you fly is the one the airport is using.
home.feat4Body: The same traffic and weather for everyone, every day, with a play streak to keep.
home.feat5Body: Each weekend one of the 50 busiest airports gets its own twist: storms, fog, rush hour or strong gusts. From version 3.3.
home.feat6Body: World boards for each airport and level: today, this week and all time. Sign in to Google Play Games for 24 achievements and seven leaderboards.
home.how1Body: Search more than 29,000 airports by code, name or city, or start with one of the 50 busiest.
home.how2Title: Draw a path to each runway
home.how2Body: Drag from each plane to a runway. Drag its tail to carry the path on, tap to circle, or draw a loop to hold.
home.how3Title: Land as many as you can
home.how3Body: Keep the planes apart and land them on the right runway. Engine failures, low fuel, storms and fog turn up as you play.
home.avLead: Short Final is a game, not a flight tracker, but the airports are real.
home.av1: Real runways, with the idents each airport uses.
home.av2: Taxiways, gates and terminals from OpenStreetMap at more than {maps} airports.
home.av3: Radio chatter in real ATC phraseology, if you switch it on in Settings.
home.av4: Closed runways show red X marks, by day and at night. Wake turbulence and runway inspections are part of the play.
home.av5: Real daylight: play Tokyo at night while it is night in Tokyo.
home.shot1: A real plane has just landed on a runway at Dallas Fort Worth, with the note Arrived from Atlanta beside it.
home.shot1Caption: A real plane lands, and says where it flew in from.
home.shot2: A runway at night, closed for an inspection: red hatched strip with X marks, and a label naming both ends.
home.shot2Caption: A closed runway shows its red X marks, by day and at night.
home.shot3: A real plane drawn towards a holding racetrack, with the track lit up under the finger.
home.shot3Caption: Draw a plane to a hold: the whole racetrack lights up under your finger.
home.shot4: A vertical video frame of the game, with the real flight names and a closing line with the score, beside the words Share a video.
home.shot4Caption: Share a 20-second video for TikTok, YouTube Shorts and Instagram Reels.
home.trailerBody: A short trailer on YouTube. The video loads only when you press play.
home.pickBody: Search more than 29,000 airports by code, name or city. Airports with a map get their own page, with runways, a map and a play button.
home.pickNone: No airport with a map matches. Try a city or a code.
home.pricingTitle: Free to play, with one optional upgrade
home.pricingBody: The daily challenge is always free. Your first 3 days are unlimited; after that you get 3 free games a day at any airport. Short Final Pro is a one-time purchase in Google Play, $2.99 at the price Google Play shows, for unlimited games.
home.faq1A: Yes. It is free on Google Play, with no ads and no account. The daily challenge is always free. Your first 3 days are unlimited; after that you get 3 free games a day at any airport. Short Final Pro is an optional one-time purchase for unlimited games.
home.faq2A: Live flights come from The OpenSky Network, with their real flight numbers. Simulated planes fill in when the sky is quiet, unless you switch on Real planes only. Short Final is a game, not a flight-tracking or navigation tool.
home.faq3A: Any of more than 29,000 airports, each with its real runways. More than {maps} also have full layouts from OpenStreetMap, with taxiways and gates, and the 50 busiest airports open offline in the app.
home.faq4Q: Can I try it without installing?
home.faq4A: Yes. The free browser demo gives you 3 free games a day, with simulated planes.
home.faq5A: Your progress stays on your phone. Ranked scores go to the online boards. If you sign in to Google Play Games, your achievements and best scores sync there. You can remove your board entries at any time.
home.faq6Q: Is the game in other languages?
home.faq6A: The game itself is in English. The Google Play page and this website are also available in 12 other languages.
home.creatorsBody: Making videos or streams about flying or games? The press kit has the facts, logos, screenshots and the trailer.
home.finalTitle: Your first landing is a tap away.
home.finalBody: Short Final is free on Google Play. No ads and no account.

press.creatorsBody: If you make videos, streams or posts about flying, air traffic or games, we would like to hear from you. We can talk about a creator challenge for your audience, for example the same daily airport for everyone to fly on the same day. We can also talk about Short Final Pro access for reviewers. We cannot promise payment, and we will say plainly what we can offer.

classroom.title: Short Final for teachers and aviation clubs
classroom.description: Short Final for classes and aviation clubs: what the free game teaches, how to use the browser demo in a lesson, and three lesson ideas.
classroom.h1: Short Final in the classroom and at the club
classroom.lead: Short Final is a free phone game about air traffic control, built on real airports. Here is what it is, why it can help a class or club, how to use the free browser demo in a lesson, and three lessons you can run with paper and one shared screen.
classroom.endTitle: Real flights are in the Android app
classroom.endBody: The browser demo plays simulated planes only. The free Android app brings in live flights from The OpenSky Network. The app is for players aged 13 and up.
classroom.contactBody: Questions about using Short Final in a class or club, or a correction to this page, go to
